scope: Living Island primer accuracy review and opt-in Island Connections advanced extension

implementation.advancedModel: Three finite island demes, fictional Seedwing birds and Shellseed plants, 24 offspring per established deme and species, up to 40 recorded generations.
mechanisms: Two distinct parents per offspring; independent diploid additive trait locus and neutral biallelic marker
Reciprocal partner-dependent breeding weights from complete pre-birth local partner distributions
Quadratic trait construction costs and explicit illustrative rainfall-dependent selection
Simultaneous distance-dependent dispersal of actual individuals; seeds use 30% of the birds’ dispersal scale
Recorded arrivals, actual migrant gametes and transmitted A/a marker copies
Finite parent sampling and allele inheritance produce drift; mutations are bidirectional and independent of environmental need
Optional six-founder Mist sample from the same ancestral pools
Private five-generation migration or reciprocal-selection comparisons retain the expedition RNG and history
interactions: Native island and species buttons, individual selector, selectable actual migrants, real parent-copy inspector and recorded offspring
Three volcanic 3D islands reuse the existing separate deterministic landscape utility; native controls and a conceptual map remain available without WebGL
Hypothetical beak/shell encounter probe changes no individuals or RNG
Recorded generation slider, exact trait history table, one-locus within and pooled genetic-diversity table
Persistent prediction and explanation drafts; dedicated journal evidence; separate advanced and primer saves

primerAudit.finding: Sound for a primer. Individuals retain born genes; offspring inherit one actual parental copy per locus. Survivor sampling and reproductive sampling are separate.
primerAudit.limitation: Three independent additive loci and non-overlapping generations omit dominance, linkage, polygenic complexity, age and sex structure.

primerAudit.finding: Mutation draws are independent of the chosen environment, with recorded bidirectional effects.
primerAudit.limitation: Mutation probability and effect size are illustrative teaching settings; they are not empirical per-nucleotide mutation rates.

primerAudit.finding: Habitat-dependent trait probabilities bias survival, while survival and parent draws remain stochastic. Equal-probability survival retains drift.
primerAudit.limitation: The survival coefficients, 2.65 offspring-per-survivor rule and 60-resident cap are not ecological calibration. One trajectory cannot attribute every shift to selection.

primerAudit.finding: Animals are fictional spriglets. Rabbit-like illustrations do not model rabbit biology. Prominent student-facing labels now explain this.
primerAudit.limitation: A real rabbit/hare version would require explicit seasonal or developmental phenotype changes where applicable, overlapping generations and species-appropriate reproduction. Snowshoe-hare seasonal molting occurs within individuals and is distinct from inherited coat differences.

primerAudit.finding: The primer gives every resident the same shared habitat. Terrain, motion, vegetation and water are decorative. Predators are a parameter, not evolving organisms.
primerAudit.limitation: It cannot test coevolution, local habitat choice, migration or reproductive isolation. The advanced model adds island-level geography and reciprocal trait effects, still with shared conditions within each island.

primerAudit.finding: Primer summary now says Trait spread (mean SD) and explains that this is not genome-wide genetic diversity.
primerAudit.limitation: The advanced neutral-marker H is a plug-in one-locus gene-diversity calculation, 2p(1-p), not observed heterozygosity or a genome-wide estimator.

teachingBoundaries: Fictional islands and species are inspired by island biogeography, not a reconstruction or forecast of a real Galápagos community.
Coevolution requires reciprocal evolutionary influence. Correlated trait lines alone do not demonstrate that mechanism; the probe and partner-effects control expose it.
Migration is not automatically successful gene flow into a new offspring cohort; actual transmitted copies are counted.
Isolation can increase between-island differences while reducing within-island diversity. It is not a promise of greater genome-wide diversity.
Divergence in one trait or marker does not establish reproductive isolation or new species.
Fixed cohort targets and relative parent-sampling weights do not model resource depletion, competition, population cycles, seed banks or ecosystem extinction risk.
A single private comparison is a stochastic demonstration, not a statistical test or a general empirical result.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Understanding Evolution — Coevolution
sources.usedFor: Reciprocal evolutionary influence between interacting species; coevolution includes multiple ecological relationships.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Understanding Evolution — Mutations
sources.usedFor: Mutations are not generated in response to what an organism needs.

sources.title: National Park Service — Snowshoe Hare
sources.usedFor: Seasonal molting changes individual coat appearance; day length triggers the cycle. This primer omits that phenotype process.

sources.title: Galápagos Conservancy — Biodiversity
sources.usedFor: Habitat and island diversity as visual and inquiry inspiration, without using dated species counts or claiming calibrated finch dynamics.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Understanding Evolution — Genetic drift
sources.usedFor: Chance variation in reproductive contributions changes allele frequencies; drift is not evidence of adaptation.

generationStory.reconstruction: Read-only reconstruction of the actual recorded round. No additional world.step, RNG draws, fabricated events or changes to history.
stages: actual parents weighted by contributed copies
generationStory.expectation: For ordered sampling of two distinct parents, expected copy share q_i = 0.5 * (w_i/W + sum_{j != i}(w_j/W * w_i/(W-w_j))). Simple normalized weights alone describe only the first parent and are incorrect for the combined inheritance expectation.
generationStory.trace: Actual parent IDs, their island before dispersal, selected trait and independently selected marker copies, pre/post-mutation values and actual transmitted A/a copies by parent origin.
generationStory.evidence: Human-readable recorded stages and origin counts saved with predictions, explanations and explicit limits. The advanced journal entry permits 12,000 characters, preserving the complete 6,000-character explanation; other note limits are unchanged.
boundaries: Conditional bookkeeping is not a unique causal decomposition.
A neutral marker has no direct effect on breeding weight; a conditional expected shift can arise through sample association with the inherited trait.
Origins identify the parent location one generation earlier, not ultimate allele ancestry.
Parent and allele-copy sampling contribute to drift; changing mean traits alone does not prove adaptation or coevolution.
No reproductive cohort with fewer than two potential parents; missing means remain undefined.
Mutation effects use actual reflected allele values, not the raw mutation draw.
